title: Holy Vedas and Holy Bible: A Comparative Study
byline: by Kanayalal M. Talreja · Rashtriya Chetana Sangathan, New Delhi · c. 2000
lede: Talreja's preface opens with quotations from missionaries hoping Hinduism will die out, from Francis Xavier to Richard Temple in 1883 to a New Zealand Anglican mission in 1993. The book is his reply. In 28 chapters he places Bible verses, quoted by book and verse from the King James Version, against Vedic mantras on the same theme. In 26 of them the Bible comes off worse. In two, on doing good and on forgiveness, he finds the scriptures agree.
facts: chapter-length comparisons, each titled “Bible does X, Vedas do Y”
chapters where Talreja finds common ground
the Trinity verse he opens with, set against Rigveda 1.164.46
the King James Bible (a Gideons printing) is his text
note: This is an apologetic work. Like many polemics, it sets the hardest Bible passages against the most elevated Vedic ones. Talreja reads the Vedas as monotheist, in the Arya Samaj tradition. Sita Ram Goel's Defence of Hindu Society criticises exactly that reading. This page summarises his contrasts and does not endorse them.

sections.title: 28 contrasts, grouped by theme
sections.lede: Our grouping of Talreja's chapter titles. The nature of God and the Bible's violence take up the most space.
items: Chapters 1, 3, 4, 5, 25, 26, 27: Trinity, a wrathful or jealous God, idols
Chapters 6, 9, 10, 13, 28: death penalty, persecution, human sacrifice
Chapters 2, 15, 19: the Virgin Mary, harsh language, damnation
Chapters 20 and 21: doing good, and forgiveness

The Vedas, says Talreja
rows: A Trinity, which he calls irrational, citing Unitarians burnt for denying it
Wrathful, jealous, vindictive, a God of massacre
A benevolent friend and father who grants mercy and bliss
Animal and human sacrifice (Isaac, Jephthah's daughter), meat, famine cannibalism
Unscientific (Joshua stops the sun), hostile to wisdom, witchcraft

sections.title: Two shared teachings
items: Vedic philosophy “urges on practical life”. Ritual without a pious life is empty, and the Bible says the same.
He quotes an Atharvaveda prayer for the prosperity even of one's enemy, alongside the Sermon on the Mount.
